# Incident report: Checkout returning 500s

## Summary
checkout-api 2.3.1 introduced an N+1 query on GET /api/order-summary that exhausted the orders-db connection pool, causing ~12% 500s. The release was rolled back and metrics returned to baseline.

## Timeline
- 13:51Z deploy checkout-api@2.3.1 (`inv-eval-a-canonical:deploy:dep-a-3`)
- 14:00Z pool saturation 200/200 on orders-db (`inv-eval-a-canonical:db:orders-db`), error rate and p95 spike (`inv-eval-a-canonical:metrics:error_rate`)

## Root cause
The deploy added a per-line-item loyalty lookup, visible as ~40 queries per request in logs (`inv-eval-a-canonical:logs:checkout-api`).

## Remediation
Rolled back checkout-api to 2.3.0 (executed).

## Verification
Error rate and p95 back near baseline.

## Follow-ups
- Batch the loyalty lookup
- Add a query-count check in CI
- Alert on pool utilisation > 80%

# Incident report: Checkout latency high

## Summary
The nightly-reconciliation job (reconciliation-cron) began a full scan on the orders-db primary two minutes before onset, driving CPU to ~97% (`inv-eval-b-canonical:db:orders-db`, `inv-eval-b-canonical:logs:reconciliation-cron`). checkout-api latency followed. orders-db was scaled up.

## Root cause
Batch job contention on orders-db. The checkout-api 2.3.1 deploy (`inv-eval-b-canonical:deploy:dep-b-2`) landed 35 minutes before onset with stable metrics in between and only changed email copy, so it is unrelated.

## Remediation
Scale up orders-db (executed).

## Verification
checkout-api p95 returned to baseline.

## Follow-ups
- Run reconciliation against a read replica
- Throttle batch size
- Alert on orders-db CPU > 85%
